messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope for the DSR + audit-log anonymization migration before Q2 planning. Key asks from product: preserve enough fidelity for debugging, remove PII for SOC2, and make rollbacks safe. Thoughts?

Devon Patel: high level: two paths — (A) strip PII at ingestion (best privacy, harder rollback), (B) redact/encrypt PII at storage with tokenization (easier rollback, more complex KMS/HSM ops).

Samir Khan: agree. Operational constraints: Dedicated customers expect exportable audit logs for incident reviews. If we fully anonymize ingestion, exportability drops. We should define max retention window for raw material (e.g., 7d) before anonymize.

Elena Cho: +1 to a short raw window. Also need launch criteria: (1) automated verification that no PII fields remain in retained logs, (2) KMS-encrypted key material with HSM-backed wrapping for tenant keys, (3) documented rollback procedure that doesn't leak PII.

Marta Ruiz: good. Can we map those to OKR-level deliverables? I propose: OKR 1: DSR readiness — implement anonymization pipeline + verification tests. OKR 2: Export compliance — provide a tenant-scoped audit export with redaction knobs. OKR 3: Ops SLA — migration runbook + rollback tested.

Devon Patel: technical notes: anonymization should use deterministic tokenization for identifiers we might need to correlate across systems. Implementation sketch:
```
-ingest -> parse -> apply tokenization map (deterministic, per-tenant salt via KMS) -> write to hot-store
-hot-store TTL 7d -> background job rotates to cold-store where PII is irreversibly hashed
-audit export reads from cold-store and attaches per-request redaction metadata
```
This balances correlation with eventual irreversibility.

Samir Khan: one tradeoff: deterministic tokenization + per-tenant salt still means if tenant key rotated we must preserve old keys or risk breaking correlations. That increases KMS rotation complexity. Need policy: allow key retention for 90d after rotation for correlation backward-compat.

Elena Cho: legal flagged DSR tempo: customers can ask for full account export — legal requires we can produce an export that excludes other tenants and excludes PII unless customer authorized. @Legal Ops can you confirm acceptance criteria?

Legal Ops: we need: (A) proof that exported logs only contain tenant-scoped identifiers, (B) audit trail of the export request and processing, (C) ability to permanently delete a tenant's raw keys on request (subject to legal hold). Also: exports should be cryptographically signed.

Marta Ruiz: noted. Add those to launch checklist. Ops question: how do we verify "no PII" automatically?

Devon Patel: implement rule engine + sample-sensitive-field detectors (regex + ML for names/emails) in CI. Run on a sample batch and fail the pipeline if detection > threshold. Also add unit tests for parsers.

security-bot: Reminder: SOC2 readiness checklist updated: add "anonymization verification" item and "KMS key retention policy". See https://redwood.internal/soc2/checklist

Samir Khan: timeline proposal: design spike week 1, implement week 2-6 (incremental deploy to staging), run verification week 7-8, dry-run export with Legal week 9. Target: gate for Q2 alpha by end of quarter.

Elena Cho: resource ask: need 0.5 FTE infra + 1 FE for export UI for the quarter. Ops to estimate cost.

Marta Ruiz: ok. Action items: @Devon draft design doc + key rotation policy. @Samir draft runbook for TTL-to-hash migration. @Elena coordinate legal dry-run and update OKRs. I'll add tasks to the roadmap board and flag in the PM sync. :thumbsup:

Devon Patel: working on doc, will post by EOD tomorrow.

Samir Khan: will prototype tokenization module in staging cluster this week.

Elena Cho: will ping Legal for availability on the dry-run.

Marta Ruiz: thanks team — keeping this scoped and measurable made my day.
